A1.justification: Despite the changed title and MMR-to-MMVU renaming, these describe the same paired-question benchmark and training-data study. Both PDFs are readable throughout their 37 pages, including figures, equations, tables and appendices; numerous retained experiments provide direct correspondences.

before.justification: V1 reports original evaluations of 18 MLLMs, instruction-tuning experiments and extensive ablations in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: V2 reports original benchmark evaluations, five-model fine-tuning comparisons, attention/logit analyses and prompting ablations, alongside retained empirical results.

M1.justification: V2 adds inference-time Content Guided Refinement, which extracts image information before answering, and Visual Attention Refinement, which modifies the image using model attention (Section 3.6 and Appendix H). These extend v1's training-data approach. The earlier Bunny architecture and training procedure remain in the supplement.

E1.justification: The same 12 visual-question categories, paired positive/negative task, training sources and general evaluation benchmarks remain. Expanding the test set and evaluating additional model and prompting configurations does not establish new task or domain coverage. Newly cited benchmarks are not reported as additional evaluations.

E2.justification: The main benchmark comparator roster changes substantially: v1's six closed and twelve open models become four and eleven in v2. Examples include replacing Claude3-Opus-V and Gemini-pro-vision with Claude3.5-Sonnet-0620 and Gemini-1.5-Pro, adding Ovis and Llama3.2-Vision, and dropping Step-1V and GLM-4V from that comparison. The older general-benchmark roster survives in the supplement.

E3.justification: The main test set expands from 300 to 893 question pairs; v2 identifies retained smaller-set experiments as preliminary evaluations. New protocols cover five-model fine-tuning, attention/logit measurements and instruction/CGR/VAR controls. RA/MR definitions and legacy training settings remain. V2's '112k pairs' wording conflicts with retained 112k dataset descriptions, so an actual doubling of training data is not established.

E4.justification: V2 adds attention-allocation and correct-answer probability analyses for LLaVA-1.6 models (Figure 4), controlled prompting ablations (Table 4), and CGR/VAR examples. These investigate mechanisms and interventions absent from v1. Earlier image-removal, data-mixture, conversation-round and data-generation prompt ablations largely remain in the supplement.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. V2's attention summaries and logit-based confidence scores are diagnostic measurements, not uncertainty estimates for experimental results.

E6.justification: V2 replaces the main leaderboard and adds substantial results. GPT-4o RA is 69.00 in v1 Table 2 and 65.06 in v2 Table 1, but the different test sets preclude interpreting this as a same-setting decline. V2 Table 2 reports InternVL2-8B tuning changing RA from 49.72 to 58.01 and MR from 30.63 to 25.04. Many legacy scores persist, while v1 Table 5's general-benchmark instruction-dataset comparison is omitted.

T1.justification: Section 3.4 adds formal definitions of token-indexed attention quantities, their aggregation and positive/negative ratios, including the confidence ratio Pneg/Ppos. These are limited mathematical additions; the original RA/MR equations remain unchanged, and neither version presents theorems or proofs.

C1.justification: V2 retains the central observation, benchmark and paired-training-data contributions, but adds attention-based explanations and inference-time prompting interventions as central contributions in its abstract, introduction and conclusion. This substantially extends v1's emphasis on evaluation and training-data remedies.

C2.justification: V2 develops the earlier visual-neglect interpretation into an explanation involving disproportionate attention to system/question tokens and reduced confidence under negative questions. Section 4.4 also explains why combining CGR and VAR may limit their individual benefits. The dataset-construction cost limitation is retained in Appendix I.

D1.justification: V2 adds inference prompts, VAR pseudocode and blending coefficients of 0.85/0.15, and clarifies that data generation implicitly occurs in one step. However, it removes v1's repository/download and metadata links, CC BY 4.0 disclosure, and datasheet/maintenance sections. Concrete resource-access information is replaced by a future-release statement; this does not establish that existing online resources were withdrawn.

R1.justification: V2 adds positioning against ConBench, NaturalBench and image-adversarial robustness research, plus references for newer evaluated models. It removes the standalone instruction-data generation survey while retaining the substantive LRV comparison. The broader distinction from accuracy and hallucination benchmarks remains.

P1.justification: The title, abstract and introduction are extensively rewritten around diagnosis and prompting. Separate benchmark, data-construction and training sections are reorganized under Methods and a substantially restructured supplement, which gains an overview and contents list. Author and affiliation information also changes.

P2.justification: V2 adopts a two-column layout, redesigns the opening examples and overview, reorganizes the benchmark illustration, and adds attention plots, prompting tables and algorithm displays. Numerous existing tables and figures are relocated and resized in the supplement; some original comparison tables are removed.

improvement.justification: The larger evaluation, five-model tuning comparison and diagnostic ablations strengthen support beyond v1's Bunny-focused training experiments. However, v2 removes substantial resource-access documentation and introduces consistency problems: VAR's masking description differs from Appendix H's inverted-map blending, and Section 4.1 gives Ovis MR as 18.60 although Table 1 reports 19.78. These empirical gains and reproducibility/consistency losses leave the net quality direction uncertain.
